headline: Litigation settlement sinks profit despite revenue growth
summary_short: IPG Photonics' Q1 2026 revenue rose 16.6% y/y to $265.5M on Industrial Solutions demand, but a $13.5M patent-litigation settlement with Trumpf pushed operating income to a $7.7M loss and cut net income to $1.6M ($0.04/diluted share) from $3.8M a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue rose 16.6% y/y to $265.5M as Industrial Solutions grew 21.0% on cutting/welding/marking demand, partly offset by a 4.7% Advanced Solutions decline. Cost of sales outgrew revenue (+20.3%, including $4.7M more in tariffs), pulling gross margin to 37.5% from 39.4% a year ago. Operating income swung to a $7.7M loss from $1.8M, driven by a $13.5M one-time Trumpf patent-litigation settlement plus higher R&D and G&A personnel costs. Net income fell to $1.6M ($0.04/diluted share) from $3.8M. Operating cash flow swung to a $5.5M outflow on higher bonus payments and working-capital investment. Cash rose to $480.8M as short-term investments matured into cash; no buybacks or dividends this quarter. No forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Industrial Solutions sales rose 21.0% y/y on higher cutting, welding, cleaning and marking demand, partly offset by lower additive manufacturing, custom, drilling and cladding sales; Advanced Solutions fell 4.7% on lower micromachining, partly offset by higher medical-laser demand.
Cost of sales grew faster than revenue (+20.3% vs +16.6%) on a $22.5M rise in cost of products sold and $4.7M more in tariffs; tariffs alone cut gross margin about 160 basis points y/y.

A $13.5M one-time patent-litigation settlement with Trumpf (none a year ago), plus higher R&D (+17.7%, mostly personnel) and G&A (+10.1%, personnel/IT/legal) expense, swung operating income to a loss.

Not explained in the release — IPG's MD&A does not discuss EBITDA; this metric is a Yahoo-provenance figure computed on a different operating-income basis than the SEC-verbatim figure this quarter (see confidence notes).
Tracks the swing to an operating loss, partly offset by an income-tax benefit of $0.6M (vs. $6.9M expense a year ago) driven by a discrete tax benefit on equity-based compensation.
Higher cash bonus payments on improved financial performance, more cash used by inventory and accounts receivable, partly offset by higher accounts payable and non-bonus accrual timing.

$110.7M of net proceeds from investment maturities moved into cash from short-term investments, partly offset by $16.3M of capex and financing outflows; a balance-sheet mix shift, not new capital raised.

Revenue grew y/y on Industrial Solutions strength but a one-time $13.5M Trumpf patent-litigation settlement, plus tariff and personnel cost inflation, pushed operating income to a loss and cut net income to $1.6M.
